explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/51: is there an infinite A ⊆ ℕ of totient values such that, with n_a the least n having φ(n) = a, n_a/a → ∞ as a → ∞? The statement asks for an infinite A and a choice n : A → ℕ with n a the least element of φ⁻¹(a), which also forces a to be a totient value. It requires n a / a → ∞ along atTop of the subtype A, i.e. as a → ∞ within A. Faithful.
